sonnet.problem: The opening card says "The people of Zion are speaking together, as one big 'we,'" and every later question repeats "the people of Zion" as the speaker. Lamentations 5:1 only says "us" and "our", and the passage title doesn't name a speaker either. The card names a speaker the passage doesn't give.
sonnet.rule: When the text doesn't say who is speaking, he doesn't guess. He uses a plain lead-in, like "Then the psalm says…", and names a speaker only when the passage or its heading does.

sonnet.problem: Stop 2 has two drawer jokes: card 5 ("I sat in the quiet at the back of a drawer for years") and card 16 ("I was a worn-out stamper in the back of a junk drawer"). That is more than one drawer joke in the same stop.
sonnet.rule: His drawer years carry a joke at most once per stop.

sonnet.problem: The card calls back to the earlier line "their fathers sinned" (Lamentations 5:7) but its verses field cites only 5:16. The citation leaves out a verse the card uses.
sonnet.rule: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
